Per our conversation last week, attached is our proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v3.pdf) that outlines 24- and 36-month reserved commit options and a couple of ramp profiles. A few items we want to confirm up front so the legal/procurement paperwork matches your expectations:

- Preferred term (12 / 24 / 36 months) you want priced as the baseline.
- Target committed baseline capacity (v100-equivalent GPUs) and expected steady-state QPS/throughput.
- Desired activation date (we can target July 1 or earlier if required; ramp plans change pricing).
- Need for burst pool (temporary capacity above committed) and whether you want a soft or hard guarantee.

Quick notes on the attachment: the pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx shows how discounts step with total committed vGPU-hours and how we handle early ramp credits. We referenced NovaHealth's expected monthly token volumes from your demo telemetry to size the pool — happy to adjust.

Thanks Hannah —

Appreciate the proposal. Procurement and our infra team reviewed the initial numbers. A few clarifications before we move to legal:

1) Term: we prefer a 24-month reserved commit as a starting point. It balances our growth assumptions and budget cycles.
2) Start date: business wants capacity available by July 1, 2027. Procurement is pushing for contract start aligned to invoice dates (they prefer July 1 as well).
3) Ramp: we cannot accept a cliff start at full capacity. We would prefer a phased ramp (baseline at t0, reach target by month 3). Please note we will require explicit ramp milestones in the contract.
4) Burst credits: we rely on occasional peaks (x30 day spikes) for reports. We need to understand how burst is priced — transient credits or a separate pool? Also request a description of how burst interacts with throughput SLAs (will it be throttled?).
5) Throughput guarantee: we need an SLO for 95th percentile latency and a throughput floor for critical endpoints — what language can you include?

Procurement is looped in (procurement@novahealth.com). Send a more prescriptive activation schedule and we can route to legal.

Elena Ruiz
VP Product, Nova Health
elena.ruiz@novahealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: Reserved commitment — activation phasing & burst allocation (internal pricing notes)

Hannah / Jordan —

Notes after reading Elena's reply and procurement signal:

- Discounting: for a 24-month firm commit we can move to a 15% list discount for the baseline committed vGPU-hours. If Nova signs within 3 weeks (by Jun 15), add an early-sign credit equal to 3% of first-year committed spend applied as service credit over Q1.
- Ramp profile: suggest we propose a tiered activation: 40% of target at day 0, 70% by 30 days, 100% by 90 days. That gives Nova a predictable invoice curve and covers steady growth.
- Burst pool: offer a shared burst pool for account-level bursts with two modes:
  * Soft-burst: best-effort extra capacity up to 12% of committed throughput, no additional charge if used < 100k tokens/month; otherwise charged at >list rate.
  * Hard-burst (paid reserve): guaranteed extra capacity for a fixed fee (added to commit).
- Throughput SLO: we can provide 95th percentile token latency guarantee for the baseline committed config on our Dedicated runtime. For burst usage, label as "best-effort" unless they buy hard-burst.

I attached a draft pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx reflecting the 15% discount and an example invoice profile. If Hannah is good with this we can send to Elena with an updated commit schedule.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks. Based on Ben's input, here's a concrete activation and commercial proposal we can put in the SOW:

Activation schedule (proposed, to be included as Exhibit A):
- Effective date / billing start: July 1, 2027.
- Day 0 (activation): 40% of contracted committed capacity live.
- Day 30: 70% of contracted capacity live.
- Day 90: 100% of contracted capacity live (target steady-state).

Burst policy:
- Shared soft-burst included: up to 12% of baseline committed throughput (best-effort). If soft-burst consumption exceeds 100k tokens/month, usage above that is billed at overflow rates (see spreadsheet).
- Hard-burst add-on available as a fixed monthly allocation if you want guaranteed extra capacity during launches.

SLOs and guarantees:
- Baseline committed capacity: 95th percentile token latency SLO (expressed per endpoint) while within committed throughput.
- Burst consumption: marked as best-effort for soft-burst; guaranteed latency only for hard-burst add-on.

Commercials:
- 24-month reserved commit with 15% off list for baseline committed vGPU-hours.
- Early-sign incentive: 3% first-year service credit if contract signed by 2027-06-15.

Attachments: redwood_commit_schedule_v2.pdf (activation diagram + milestone table).

If that aligns, we'll prepare the SOW + DocuSign packet and include Exhibit A with the schedule. Ben will prepare the final invoice profile.

Best,
Hannah
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
